subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should the Gateway reject generic `sessions.subscribe` for browser-copilot clients, or extend every transcript/tool subscription delivery path to require the copilot’s authoritative per-tab allowlist?
rationale: Both approaches affect the permanent Gateway subscription contract; the PR’s confidentiality goal makes an unscoped compatibility path unsafe, but maintainers must choose the durable public boundary.

options.title: Reject broad copilot subscriptions
options.body: Allow the browser copilot only through its Gateway-owned per-tab allowlist and leave generic subscriptions for existing clients unchanged.

options.title: Scope every event path
options.body: Retain generic subscription calls but require every transcript and tool-event broadcast to carry and enforce its canonical session key.

recommendation.title: Reject broad copilot subscriptions
recommendation.body: Allow the browser copilot only through its Gateway-owned per-tab allowlist and leave generic subscriptions for existing clients unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR’s Gateway admission and delivery design is concentrated in this author’s security-contract commits.
